title: I Returned the Expired Rain Check With the Manager's Initials

parts.text: I brought a rain check to register 3 at 5:40 p.m. The cashier said it expired yesterday. The date was smudged. The initials were the manager's, from a day he had promised me the sale price whenever the water came back. I was forty-six, holding canned tomatoes that were no longer on sale. I asked for the manager. He arrived, recognized his R.M., and said policy was the printed day. I pointed at the smudge that his own pen had made. He honored it, once, and announced rain checks would be printed by the computer now. I paid the sale price. Tomatoes rolled in the cart like a small legal victory. Initials are signatures. Smudges are still ink. I do not need a second rain check. I needed this one. The computer can have the next flood.

social.video_title: His initials outlived the smudged date — Part 1/1
social.description: Register 3, promised sale, R.M. on paper. Computers got the job. Would you have accepted yesterday?
